title: Dorchester: a 22-year-old mixed development ahead of its time.
location: Plaza Damas, Sri Hartamas, Kuala Lumpur
excerpt: An older apartment block within the Plaza Damas mixed development, with shops, offices and a mall at its door. Sean admires the address, the integration and the spacious unit, but flags leaks, old structure and noise.
takeaways: An 880 sq ft two-bedroom asks about RM520,000 and rents for about RM3,000 refurbished.
Shops, cafes, a convenience store, offices and Hartamas Shopping Centre are all under cover nearby.
Deep beams, big columns, leaks in common areas and a low corridor show its age.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Dorchester is the residential part of Plaza Damas, built about 22 years ago as a mixed development of shop offices, offices, Hartamas Shopping Centre, a hotel and apartments, long before Publika. Each floor has about 32 units along a hotel-style corridor with two fast lifts. The common areas are dated, with leaks, a basic gym and a pool reached by stairs, though maintenance work is under way.

Sean viewed a refurbished 880 sq ft two-bedroom corner unit with a 3.2 m ceiling in the main areas, a 3.85 m-wide living room, two large bedrooms sharing one bathroom and a balcony that wraps around about 270 degrees. Columns about 680 mm wide and beams almost 1 m deep cut across the rooms, and windows cover only about a third of the facade.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: Plaza Damas sits in Sri Hartamas, between Mont Kiara, Dutamas and Publika and close to Damansara Heights, with highways to PJ and the city. Residents and office workers from many countries fill its cafes, restaurants, bars, tuition centres and the shopping centre's banquet halls, all within covered walking distance. Traffic around the plaza is heavy.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Listings ask about RM520,000 for this 880 sq ft unit type, and studio units sell for far less than newer projects nearby. A fully refurbished unit asks about RM3,000 a month, where Sean says a modern unit of this size nearby would rent for about RM5,000. Kuala Lumpur City Hall does not allow units to be partitioned into extra rooms.

standout.title: Publika before Publika
standout.body: Shops, offices, a hotel, a mall and apartments were woven together here before the Strata Titles Act made such divisions clear. From your unit you can walk under cover to a convenience store, a cafe or a tuition centre, which Sean calls a true mixed development decades ahead of its time.

pros: The address: between Mont Kiara, Damansara Heights and Dutamas with Publika, connected to PJ and new highways, and a business hub whose international crowd forms the tenant pool.
The mixed development: like a 22-year-old Publika, with Plaza Damas, Dorchester, Mayfair, hotels and a shopping centre integrated, so almost everything is within covered walking distance.
The unit: an 880 sq ft two-bedroom that is wide, long and high, a rare 270-degree balcony, and touches such as a kitchen opening to the living room and two windows in the corner bedroom.
cons: Maintenance: leaks in the gym, pool and corridors from pipes that weren't well coordinated, so refurbishment takes real work and steady maintenance collection.
The mixed development's downside: unclear boundaries between who maintains what, and noise and bustle that make it no place for peace, especially on lower floors.
Old design: huge columns and deep beams that restrict layouts, no en-suite master bathroom, a dense hotel-style floor with two lifts, and steps to the pool with little thought for accessibility.

closing: A charming, convenient bargain for people working nearby, provided the unit is refurbished; Sean says he wouldn't mind owning one.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this October 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the unit; floor plans weren't available, so the size and prices are from listings as he quoted them. The Makeover Guys, where Sean works, refurbished the unit.
